v: avya॰ praTa--qa । 1 AramBe 2 gatO 3 utkarze 4 prATamye 5 sarvatoBAve 6 utpattO, 7 KyAtO 8 vyavahAre ca puruzottamaH । asya kriyAyoge upasargatvam । gatitvaYca । asyArTaBedo dAharaRAni gaRaratnawI॰ uktAni yaTA “pra AdikarmadIrDeSaBfSasamBavatfptiviyogaSudDiSaktIcCASAntipUjAgradarSanezu” prayAtaH । pravAlamUzikaH praBurdeSasya । pravadanti dAyAdAH । himavato gaNA praBavati । praBuktamannam । prozitaH । prasannaM jalam । praSaktaH । prArTayate । praSAnto'gniH । prAYjali । prabAlam । pralokayati” ।
m: forward, in front, on, forth (mostly in connection with a verb, esp. with a verb of motion which is often to be supplied; sometimes repeated before the verb, cf. Pāṇ. viii, 1, 6; rarely as a separate word, e.g. AitBr. ii, 40)
as a prefix to subst. = forth, away, cf. प्र-वृत्ति, प्र-स्थान
as pref. to adj. = excessively, very, much, cf. प्र-चण्ड, प्र-मत्त
in nouns of relationship = great- cf. प्र-पितामह, प्र-पौत्र
(according to native lexicographers it may be used in the senses of गति, आ-रम्भ, उत्-कर्ष, सर्वतो-भाव, प्राथम्य, ख्याति, उत्-पत्ति, व्य्-अवहार), RV.; &c.
प्र [cf. पुरस्, पुरा, पूर्व; Zd. fra; Gk. πρό; Lat. pro; Slav. pra-, pro-; Lith. pra-; Goth. faúr, faúra; Germ. vor; Eng. fore.]
2. प्र mfn. (√ पॄ or प्रा) filling, fulfilling
(n. fulfilment ifc.; cf. आकूति-, कक्ष्य-, काम-)
a: प्र — ind. 1 As a prefix to verbs it means ‘forward’, ‘forth’, ‘in front’, ‘onward’, ‘before’, ‘away’, as in प्रगम्, प्रस्या, प्रचर्, प्रय &c. --2 With adjectives it means ‘very’, ‘excessively’, ‘very much’ &c: प्रकृष्ट, प्रमत्त &c., see further on. --3 With nouns whether derived from verbs or not, it is used in the following senses according to G. M.:-- (a) beginning, commencement; (प्रमाणं, प्रस्थानं, प्रह्ण); (b) length; ( प्रवालभूषिक); (c) power (प्रभु); (d) intensity, excess; (प्रवाद, प्रकर्ष, प्रच्छाय, प्रगुण); (e) source or origin; (प्रभव, प्रपौत्र); (f) completion, perfectness, satisfaction (प्रभुक्तमन्नं); (g) destitution, separation, being without; (प्रोषिता, प्रपर्णवृक्षः); (h) apart; (प्रज्ञु); (i) excellence; (प्राचार्यः): (j) purity (प्रसन्नं जलं); (k) wish (प्रार्थना); (l) cessation (प्रशम); (m.) adoration, respect; (प्रांजलिः who respectfully folds his hands together); (n.) prominence (प्रणस, प्रवाल). In the Veda it is often used as a separable adverb.
